text:
Sam: Heads-up: Orchid Systems wants a Private POC today. They asked for VPC peering (control plane in our acct) + a small NAT for outbound. Need exact route/security steps to hand to their cloud engineer.

Maya: Quick checklist: customer CIDRs, peering vs PrivateLink choice, control-plane ENI subnet CIDRs, route table IDs to update, and NAT IPs for egress allowlisting. Do we have Orchid CIDRs?

Sam: SOW lists 10.40.0.0/16 (apps) and 10.41.128.0/18 (onprem). They prefer peering.

Ravi: On their side add: destination=10.200.0.0/16 -> peering-conn-id. Our side: destination=10.40.0.0/16 -> peering-conn-id. Confirm no CIDR overlap. Also enable DNS resolution on the peering connection.

Maya: Important: they must not import a 0.0.0.0/0 route via propagation into the peered RTBs. If they use a NAT for egress, send us the NAT IPs so we can whitelist them in our outbound policies.

Nora: Security items: allow TCP 443 from their peered subnets to our control-plane ENIs. If they want strict IPs we can provide ENI addresses, otherwise allow the peered CIDR with justification. Add cert fingerprint for mTLS where requested in the questionnaire.

Ravi: Pasteable example for their cloud engineer: on their side: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd1234 --destination-cidr-block 10.200.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c3d
On our side: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0ffff2222 --destination-cidr-block 10.40.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c3d
Also run modify-vpc-peering-connection-options to allow DNS resolution. Replace IDs.

Maya: Recommend dedicating two /24s for control-plane ENIs and one /24 for model egress/NAT. Security groups: only HTTPS to control plane, temporary SSH if needed for debugging.

Nora: For the security questionnaire answer: "We require VPC peering (or PrivateLink) with explicit route entries to the control plane CIDR; TLS 1.2+ enforced; mutual TLS recommended for production."

Sam: If they ask for PrivateLink instead, any major POC blockers?

Ravi: PrivateLink works but requires them to provision interface endpoints in each AZ and accept our service name. More DNS/SG work but avoids route changes. For a fast POC peering is usually quicker.

deploy-bot: Note: automated rollout will wait until peering is accepted.

Sam: I'll send this to Orchid and request their route table IDs and NAT IPs. Thanks team.
